title: Hall Burger Bar
shortDescription: Smash burgers with toppings bar for ten
subtitle: Smash burgers with toppings bar for ten
description: Beef balls are smashed on a hot griddle into thin crispy patties, then served with toasted buns and a full toppings bar—lettuce, tomato, onion, pickles, bacon, and multiple cheeses. Crew assembles at the line.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Hall Burger Bar in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep toppings and bacon
steps.instruction: Cook bacon on a wire rack at 400°F until crisp, about 18 minutes. Slice and arrange all burger bar toppings in labeled hotel pans while bacon cooks. Target oven/smoker temperature: 400°F.

steps.title: Form beef balls
steps.instruction: Divide beef into loose 3-ounce balls without compacting—tight balls resist smashing and cook unevenly. Season the griddle surface lightly with salt.

steps.title: Smash and sear patties
steps.instruction: Heat griddle ripping hot. Place balls on surface, smash flat with a sturdy spatula within 10 seconds, and sear 2 minutes until deep brown crust forms on the bottom.

steps.title: Flip, cheese, and finish
steps.instruction: Scrape and flip patties, add cheese, and cook 1 minute until cheese melts and internal temp reaches 160°F. Toast buns on the griddle during the last minute.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Open the burger bar
steps.instruction: Transfer patties to a warm holding pan. Line up buns, patties, bacon, cheeses, and toppings. Call crew to build custom burgers while patties are still hot.

proTips: Use parchment over the patty when smashing if your spatula sticks to raw beef.
One slice of cheese on the patty plus one on the bun top doubles melt coverage.
Keep a sheet pan under the griddle edge to catch grease and simplify cleanup.
tonightSpread: Smash burger bar with bacon, cheese, and full condiment station.
Oven fries or tater tots seasoned with ranch powder for classic diner vibes.
leftovers: Chop patties into a cheeseburger mac bake with pasta and cheddar.
Crumble cold patties over salad for a hearty lunch bowl.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Burger bar night is democratic—pickles but no onions, double bacon, triple cheese, all acceptable. Smash technique delivers diner-quality crust in minutes on a flat-top or cast-iron.
mealPrepNotes: Form loose 3-ounce beef balls ahead and refrigerate on a sheet pan. Pre-slice all toppings into hotel pans. Cook bacon in the oven on racks while burgers smash on the griddle.
